rca_result_structured.primary_cause_text: [E1] The centrifugal compressor K-101 tripped due to two primary issues: high journal bearing temperature and discharge overpressure. According to the operating procedure and manual, the system automatically trips when the journal bearing temperature exceeds 95.0 °C or discharge pressure surpasses 450.0 PSI. In this case, the journal bearing temperature was the primary cause, triggering the overpressure trip. The discharge pressure was a secondary indicator, but the main issue was the elevated temperature. The system's response was appropriate as per the operating procedure.

5.1 Immediate Automated Response to Overpressure Surge:
If discharge pressure exceeds 450.0 PSI (31.02 bar) or bearing temperature breaches 95.0 °C:
1. The automated safety interlock trips breaker VCB-101A, de-energizing the main 450 kW drive motor.
2. Emergency Safety Relief Valve SV-402 opens fully, venting trapped hydrocarbon volume into the Flare-Header.
3. Minimum recirculation bypass valve opens 100% to dissipate residual hydraulic momentum.
